<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via SharingRuleService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via expandRecipient (symbol, a method of class SharingRuleService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1ffc4c54d31485b1d8525573da37bdde4756a2a6` — the merge of head `f9c4e48bb719c84107f3e6f4374da957b19f96b8` into base `87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1ffc4c54d31485b1d8525573da37bdde4756a2a6 && git checkout 1ffc4c54d31485b1d8525573da37bdde4756a2a6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337 f9c4e48bb719c84107f3e6f4374da957b19f96b8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337 && git merge --no-ff f9c4e48bb719c84107f3e6f4374da957b19f96b8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review: #31734 (E4 Q1 follow-up), head 20a19d69 · 2026-11-09T03:59Z**

Verdict: **PASS, once the one declaration below is in.** No re-review is needed.

| Red line | Reading |
|---|---|
| 1. Never loosens | `resolveQueue` / `expandMembers` / `isMember` take an optional `callerPackageId`. Without it, the read is environment-wide as before. With it, the read is D3 from the rule's package: own, then the unique holder in the declared closure plus `sys`, then a refusal. The D-and-U case now resolving to D is the target D3 answer, which E4's interim refused on purpose ("stricter than D3, never looser", 6729421618). It is not a loosening. |
| 2. Ambiguity reported, never guessed | It goes only through `resolvePackageScopedName`, with no first-registered fallback. Two holders in the closure are refused `ambiguous-in-closure`, naming both (409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` under refuse). Ablations A1–A3 are red. |
| 3. Independently releasable | `Clause-②: yes (widening)` for the optional contract key, and an implementation written before it still satisfies the contract. Gates 94/94, plugin-sharing 1493/1493, dogfood VERDICT 0. |

**Required declaration:**
- Deviation (1) is a narrowing: a disabled dependency D, with an unrelated U holding the name, used to serve U's queue to P's rule and now serves nobody. That is the right D3 answer, since U is outside the closure, but the changeset's "every other answer is unchanged" does not cover it.
- Add it to the PR body's `Narrowing:` line and to the changeset, with the first-party count of 0.
- Make sure the refusal is reported with U named (`outside-closure`), not silent.

**Accepted:**
- (2) The position look-through over every declared holder.
- (3) The name `OwnershipQueueCallerPackage`, the seat's call.

**(4) Carrier:** yes, file the card. Assignment rules and approval steps still read package-written queue names environment-wide, which is stricter than D3. That is the same interim shape, and the reads should pass the declaring package's id. The card is `domain:server`, `Part of #31527`, `Blocked-by: #31734`.

Seat 3 accepts and lands this after the declaration and green CI. It is not a governed surface: `packages/spec` contracts are not on the governed list.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review, final: #31734, head f9c4e48b · 2026-11-09T04:33Z**

Verdict: **PASS.** I re-read the source change in d1d77686.

`listedHoldersView` takes disabled packages out of the holder set before the resolver runs. That is the same population `listItems` serves, which E4's readers already bound to (6729421618), so a disabled package is never a holder here, neither for an answer nor for ambiguity.
- The case of a disabled dependency D with an unrelated U holding the name now reaches the resolver's own `outside-closure` refusal naming U: a 409 under `refuse`, both loggers warn once, and U gains no grant.
- Before this change, the read resolved to D and was then discarded as hidden, which reported nothing.
- The pin is cited in the `Narrowing:` line, and ablations A4, A5 and A6 are red.

Seat 3 accepts and lands this after green CI, with CI's Dogfood Regression Gate standing in for a local re-run. It is not a governed surface.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31789 (Fixes #31734, ADR-0150 E4 follow-up) · 2026-11-09T05:10Z

Head-sha: `f9c4e48bb719c84107f3e6f4374da957b19f96b8`

- **Form:** draft to `main`. The first content line is `Fixes #31734`, and the whole card lands here. `Clause-②: yes (widening); narrowing per ADR-0150 D3 declared below`. `Metadata-protocol: none`, because a service-contract change is not a metadata-protocol change (#31424 rule 2, triage 6729669463).
- **Premise measured:** `IOwnershipQueueService`'s `resolveQueue`, `expandMembers` and `isMember` take an optional `callerPackageId` (`OwnershipQueueCallerPackage`). Without it the read stays environment-wide, as before; a legacy implementation still compiles, and that is pinned. plugin-sharing passes the rule's package on the recompute, the per-user pass and the BU look-through, and it resolves only through objectql's `resolvePackageScopedName`: there is no second resolver and no first-registered fallback. `listedHoldersView` drops disabled packages before the resolver runs. E4's P-side check still runs first.
- **Pins and ablations:** the card's D-and-U case resolves to D's queue, red on `main`. Two holders in the closure are refused, naming both. A caller with no package reads as today. The disabled-D/U case refuses `outside-closure` naming U: 409 under `refuse`, and each logger warns once. Ablations went red: A1/A2/A3 (1/1/9) and A4/A5/A6 (2/1/1), each restored.
- **Gates (check-runs on this head):** 70 runs, 57 success, 13 skipped, 0 other. `check-governed-merges --pr 31789`: NOT governed, 523 changed lines. K = 28 first-parent commits on `main` since the PR base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 94/94 exit 0. plugin-sharing: 1493/1493. Full dogfood on `20a19d69`: 3652 passed. The only behaviour moved after that, the disabled-D/U refusal, reaches no first-party package (0 queues), and CI's Dogfood Regression Gate covers this head.
- **Accepted deviations, each a seat ruling:**
  1. Disabled D with an unrelated U: main served U's queue silently; now a D3 refusal naming U. Declared as the Narrowing line, first-party 0.
  2. `queuesNaming` looks through every declared holder.
  3. The new public name `OwnershipQueueCallerPackage`.
  4. One forced test edit: the spec pin's option keys include `callerPackageId`.
- **Epic red-line review:** final PASS at this head, after the conditional PASS on `20a19d69`.
- **Out of scope:** filed #31790 (assignment rules and approval steps pass the declaring package; Blocked-by #31734).
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31734, `pm:dispatched` removed, and the card closed by `Fixes`. #31790 is then unblocked.
